discovery: Native MCP: scene.architecture request:{command:operators,operator:<id>}. Read current engine capabilities and operator contracts before composing. These examples explain concepts; connected-engine schemas are authoritative.

items.title: Shape a surface
items.summary: Create a curved petal, leaf, panel or roof from a shared profile. Shape belongs to parameters, not a species name.

items.title: Start with a solid
items.summary: Compose cubes, spheres, cylinders, cones or planes; assign a reusable material role.

items.title: Connect two points
items.summary: Build a support between explicit endpoints. A recipe can compute each endpoint from its surroundings.

items.title: Name a connection
items.summary: Expose a stable point for another assembly to attach to or reference.

items.title: Arrange many parts
items.summary: Repeat a node with stable indices. Use @i and @j in expressions to choose each piece's placement.

items.title: Articulate a part
items.summary: Animate a part around an axis without rebuilding its topology every frame.

items.title: Calculate a relationship
items.summary: Combine bounded numeric expressions and parameters. For example, double a length or arrange pieces around a circle.

items.title: Declare the surroundings
items.summary: Reference a named support, path or assembly anchor. Relationships are explicit and local.

items.title: Reuse a calculation
items.summary: Give a bounded expression a name, then reference it as %half. This keeps a recipe readable.

items.title: Sample the surroundings
items.summary: Sample height on a declared cube support, or signed distance from a support footprint or path corridor. Arbitrary mesh terrain is not covered.

items.title: Leave room
items.summary: Conditionally emit a piece. Zero skips it; one keeps it. Include a piece's whole footprint when reserving clearance.
